name: Anastrozole
mechanism: Non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor - blocks conversion of androgens to oestrogens in peripheral tissues, reducing circulating oestrogen levels by ~80% in postmenopausal women
dosing: Breast cancer: 1mg OD continuously for 5 years (some evidence for extended therapy). Can be taken with/without food. Continue until tumour progression or unacceptable toxicity
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, premenopausal women (unless ovarian suppression), severe hepatic/renal impairment. Only for oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer
interactions: Tamoxifen (reduces anastrozole efficacy - don't combine). Oestrogen-containing therapies (antagonizes effect). Warfarin (monitor INR). No significant CYP450 interactions
monitoring: Bone mineral density (DEXA) at baseline and every 2 years - treat osteoporosis if present. Lipid profile (may ↑ cholesterol). LFTs at baseline. Assess menopausal status (must be postmenopausal). Monitor for bone pain, fractures, arthralgia
pregnancy: Contraindicated - teratogenic. May cause fetal harm. Premenopausal women must use non-hormonal contraception. Check not pregnant before starting
sideEffects: Very common: arthralgia/bone pain (affect joints/back), hot flushes, osteoporosis/fractures, asthenia, headache. Common: vaginal dryness, hair thinning, GI upset, myalgia, hypercholesterolaemia, mood changes, skin rash. Rare: hepatitis, allergic reactions, thromboembolic events (less than tamoxifen)
pharmacokinetics: Well absorbed orally, 85% oral bioavailability. Peak levels 2h. Half-life: 40-50h. Steady state in 7 days. Hepatic metabolism (85%), renal excretion. Food doesn't affect absorption
clinicalPearls: First-line adjuvant therapy for postmenopausal ER+ breast cancer (superior to tamoxifen in some trials). Lower thromboembolic risk than tamoxifen but higher fracture risk. Arthralgia is most common side effect causing discontinuation - may improve with switching to different AI or taking at night. Calcium and vitamin D supplementation essential. Bisphosphonates if osteoporosis or high fracture risk. Extended therapy beyond 5 years controversial - discuss risks/benefits. If on tamoxifen, switch after 2-3 years to complete 5 years AI therapy. Monitor for cardiovascular risk factors as oestrogen-protective effect lost
indication: Postmenopausal oestrogen receptor-positive early/advanced breast cancer (adjuvant, first-line, or second-line after tamoxifen)
